cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to talk about JavaScript objects.
As we mentioned before, in JavaScript there is input objects which can be used as hash table.
So here I'm going to show you how can we use the JavaScript objects as hash table.
Now we have learned that hash table is a data structure that stores the key and value pairs in an array
based on the hash function, and we can do the same thing by using the object.
Now, to be able to create the object in JavaScript we are just going to use the curly braces.
So here all we have to do is we're just going to create hash table like this equals to curly braces.
If I write this it's just going to create an empty object called hash table.
Now objects use the technique of hashing for storing the elements in hash table.
When property is added to JavaScript object, the property name which is key is hashed using hash function.
And this is going to generate an index where we are going to use that index to store the key and value
pairs in array.
If two different keys generate the same hash code, it leads to hash collision, and based on the JavaScript
engine, it's going to use the different strategies to handle hash collisions.
Typically, it's going to either use separate chaining or open addressing.
This is going to depend on the JavaScript engine that it uses, and based on that, it's going to optimize
the process to ensure the efficient property access and management.
So to be able to insert the element in this hash table that we have created using objects, all we have
to do is we're just going to put the hash table name.
Then we are going to put the square brackets.
So in our case as you remember we were putting the apple for example.
And we are going to put equal 20.
Now we can go ahead and add another for orange as well.
So in this case it's going to be ten.
So let's say if these two keys generates the same hash code in this case it's going to use the collision
techniques based on the JavaScript engine.
Not to be able to access the values of the this key and value pair that we have inserted over here.
All we have to do is we're just going to put hash table with square brackets.
Then we have to provide over here the key now to be able to see it in the console.
I'm just going to put the console log like this.
Now if I just go ahead and run our code you will see that the value of the Apple key is 20.
Now we can just go ahead and print out the hash table itself to the console.
So if I just put it like this, you will see that here we have key with the apple and the value is 20.
And we have another key with orange and its value is ten.
So that's how we are creating and inserting the elements in the objects for hash table.
Now to be able to check that if the key exists in the hash table, all we have to do is we're just going
to use the in operator.
So here inside the quotes I'm just going to put Apple in.
Then all we have to do is we just put the hash table.
So I'm just going to delete this part.
Now if I run this you will see that in this case it's going to return.
True because this is exists.
Now if I put over here for example, here and run our code, you will see that in this case it's false
because P is not exist in this hash table over here.
Now to be able to retrieve the keys we are going to use the object keys.
So here we can do it like this.
Let keys is equal to object dot keys.
And as a parameter we are just going to pass hash table like this.
Now if I just go ahead and run our code you will see that in this case nothing happens.
We can just go ahead and put over here keys and you will see that it's printing out the array of the
keys to the console like this.
So Apple is the first key and the orange is the second key.
Now it's possible to remove the elements from the object.
So we can do it by using the delete function.
So here all we have to do is we're just going to put like this delete.
Then we are just going to access the hash table.
And inside the square brackets we're just going to put the key.
So if I put over here key and run our code you will see that it returns true because it deletes that.
And if I just go ahead and print out hash table to the console, you will see that in this case we have
only one key value pair over here.
Because we have successfully deleted key and value pair from the hash table.
Now these are the common operations that we can do with the hash table using the objects.
So with this short lecture I explained objects as hash tables in JavaScript.
Now in the next lecture we are going to use the another built in object in JavaScript, which is map
and map object also can be used as hash table.
So we are going to implement it in the next lecture and see the differences between map objects as a
hash table and objects as hash table.
So see you in the next lecture.
